source_text:
ἀμαυροῦν οὐ δυνήσεται τάφος· πάντων γὰρ αὐτῆς οὐδαμῶς λάθοι στόμα καλὸν
φερούσης νουθέτημα τῷ βίῳ· εἰ δ' οὖν, λαλήσει καὶ γραφὴ πάντων πλέον αὕτη παρ'
αὐτὸν τὸν τάφον τεθειμένη.
thought_title: The tomb cannot darken Anna's lesson
orientation: Arethas is concluding his praise of Anna, arguing that her grave cannot hide the virtue her life taught.
pass_a_gloss: The tomb will not be able to darken it; for by no means would the beautiful mouth of her, who carries a lesson for life, escape the notice of all; but if not, the inscription itself, placed beside the very tomb, will speak more than all.

choices.why: Keeps the visual metaphor of obscuring light or brightness, matching the earlier imagery of shining crowns and boldness.
Literal rendering preserves the personification of Anna's speech or reputation as a mouth that cannot be hidden.
Uses the fixed glossary term 'lesson' and keeps the dative as indicating the lesson's purpose or sphere.
In context this refers to the written epitaph on the tomb, not Scripture or writing in general.
Preserves the comparative force: the inscription will speak more than all other things.

pass_b_english: The tomb will not be able to darken these things. For the beautiful mouth that carries a lesson for life could never escape notice. And if it should, the inscription placed beside the tomb itself will speak more than all.

last_rejected.source_quote: στόμα καλὸν φερούσης νουθέτημα τῷ βίῳ
last_rejected.why: "στόμα" refers to Anna's person/reputation, not literal mouth; "beautiful mouth" is absurd here.
last_rejected.fix: her noble reputation that bears a lesson for life could never escape notice
last_rejected.ruling: στόμα καλὸν is standard praise of speech/eloquence; 'beautiful mouth' is literal but within normal range, not absurd mistranslation.

problems.quote: the inscription placed beside the tomb itself will speak more than all
problems.why: 'More than all' is vague—more than what? Likely 'more than all else' or 'more than any voice.'
problems.fix: Use 'will speak louder than anything else.'

edits.old: the inscription placed beside the tomb itself will speak more than all.
edits.new: the inscription placed beside the tomb itself will speak louder than anything else.

fixed: Changed 'more than all' to 'louder than anything else' to clarify the comparison in πάντων πλέον.

problems.quote: The tomb will not be able to darken these things
problems.why: Same shift continues; 'these things' refers back across section break with unclear antecedent.
problems.fix: Indicate author continues speaking of Anna.

edits.old: The tomb will not be able to darken these things.
edits.new: The tomb will not be able to darken her.

fixed: The source has ἀμαυροῦν οὐ δυνήσεται τάφος, with the object implied from the preceding context about Anna's virtue; 'these things' had no clear antecedent, so 'her' restores the reference to Anna.
